post.description: Run one sweep now ("Run rules now"): read the runners, evaluate every rule, raise and send what is new.

Exchange the control plane JWT (in Authorization header) for a session
cookie scoped to this Workspace subdomain.

The cookie carries the same JWT, just delivered as a Secure HttpOnly cookie
so the browser sends it automatically on same-origin XHR/fetch and on
WebSocket upgrades (where Authorization headers can't be set by JS).

CurrentUser only proves who the *gateway* says the caller is; it does not
vouch for this Authorization header. Because the token is persisted and
the session's credential (no service receives it any more: X-001 delegated tokens), it is verified here
against the control-plane JWKS (signature, issuer, audience, expiry, org)
and must belong to the same subject and org as the trusted gateway identity.
A token that fails either check is never stored (W-003).

The cookie expires when the JWT expires; the SPA must call /exchange
again with a freshly refreshed JWT.

Clear the session cookie — always (W-004).

Logging out must work with an expired, malformed or missing credential: that is exactly when a stale cookie needs clearing, and
an endpoint that answers 401 before deleting it leaves the cookie in the browser. So this route requires no authentication; the
identity and the audit event are best-effort extras (an unverifiable caller simply is not audited), and the cookie is deleted
with the attributes it was set with whatever happens. Idempotent: logging out twice, or without a session, is a 200.

get.description:
Return the current principal, the local user mirror and the caller's Workspace permissions.

Called by the SPA on load. Needs only a gateway-verified caller (not `workspace:access:view`), so a user without access

post.description:
Mint a single-use, short-lived ticket for the WebSocket handshake.

Browsers can't attach the session cookie's Authorization-header
equivalent on a WS upgrade in every deployment topology, so the caller
still has to identify itself via the query string — but a raw bearer JWT
there (the previous design) is a long-lived credential that infra/proxy
logs can capture. This ticket is worthless beyond one connection
attempt: bound to exactly this org+user+session, deleted from Redis the
instant the gateway reads it (single-use), and expired after
WS_TICKET_TTL_SECONDS regardless (WS-AUTH-010).

Ownership of `session_id` is verified here, at mint time — the gateway
trusts a presented ticket's binding rather than re-querying the DB, since
the ticket itself is the delegated proof of that already-made decision.

get.description:
Return the fully materialized result of an execution from persisted
output chunks — a reliable REST fallback to the WebSocket stream.

For SQL: { status, columns:[{name,type}], rows:[[...]], row_count, ... }
and, for a script of several statements, `results`: one entry per statement
({statement, sql, columns, rows, row_count, truncated, status, error}); the top-level
columns/rows are then the last statement that returned a result set.
For notebook cells: the same envelope plus `outputs`, an ordered list of
Jupyter output chunks ({output_type, payload}) — stream / display_data /
execute_result / error — so the client can render cell output faithfully.

post.description:
Receive PR / push events from the Git provider.

Real impl:
  1. Verify signature via provider.verify_webhook(headers, body)
  2. Parse event, identify affected workspace by repo_full_name
  3. Publish event to Redis on session channels of users watching the workspace

An unverifiable webhook is rejected with 401 — including every webhook
for a provider whose secret isn't configured outside dev (WS-GIT-009).

post.description:
Create a workspace bound to a Git repository and import its files.

This is what the 'Create workspace from Git repository' modal calls — one
request instead of the two-step create-then-bind flow. State is made
durable in steps (WS-GIT-009):
  1. workspace + binding(status='provisioning') are COMMITTED before the
     clone starts — visible to other requests, and a crash mid-clone
     leaves an honest 'provisioning' row rather than nothing;
  2. the clone+import runs under the workspace Git lock;
  3. the final status — 'ready', or 'failed' with status_reason — is
     committed. Any per-file import error or hitting the workspace file
     limit ends in 'failed', with the affected files listed.

post.description:
Commit dirty files to the bound Git working copy.

Workflow:
  1. Resolve workspace + binding (must be 'ready', remote re-validated).
  2. Under the workspace Git lock: materialize the local working copy.
  3. Read every dirty file's content from object storage.
  4. Write into the working copy, stage, commit.
  5. Mark committed files as no-longer-dirty in metadata; record commit sha.
  6. Audit.

Pull the remote branch and re-import changed files into the workspace.

Any file that couldn't be re-imported (or the workspace file limit) is
reported: the response says ``"status": "pulled_with_errors"`` and lists
the files, and the binding goes to 'failed' with them in status_reason —
commit/push then refuse until a clean pull, so a commit can't write the
stale workspace copy of those files back over the remote's. A clean pull
sets the binding (back) to 'ready'.

token to the secrets backend, and record a GitCredential reference row.

`state` is consumed (deleted) the instant it's read — a captured or
replayed callback URL can't be used twice, and a state that never
existed or already expired fails closed rather than silently proceeding
unauthenticated.

`state` and the PKCE `code_verifier` are generated here, never handed to
the caller, and stored server-side (Redis, single-use, 10-minute TTL)
keyed by `state` — the callback re-derives everything it needs from that
row rather than trusting anything else the browser brings back.

get.description:
Readiness for k8s: every dependency this pod can't serve without —
the metadata DB, Redis (WebSocket fan-out, tickets, execution wake-ups),
the blob store, and the in-process execution worker when this pod runs
